questions.prompt: A page only needs the server to push notification events. Which browser API directly provides that one-way stream?

choices.text: EventSource for server-sent events.
A bidirectional WebSocket as the only possible solution.
A synchronous XMLHttpRequest that waits on the main thread.
Polling a local cache without making any server requests.

questions.explanation: EventSource receives server-sent events. WebSocket can also serve realtime needs but is not the only option and has a different directionality.

sources.title: WebSocket API
sources.claim: WebSocket supports sending and receiving while EventSource server-sent events provide one-way server-to-client events.

questions.prompt: An SSE response emits fields but never terminates an event block with a blank line. Which detail is missing?

choices.text: A separate JSON-RPC request for every field.
A WebSocket masking key on each text line.
A Content-Length header equal to the eventual size of the unlimited stream.
The delimiter ending a complete event.

questions.explanation: SSE events are text blocks separated by a pair of newlines. JSON-RPC, WebSocket framing and database markers are different protocols.

sources.title: Using server-sent events
sources.claim: SSE uses text/event-stream with blank-line-separated events; retry specifies milliseconds and EventSource reconnects after disconnection.

questions.prompt: An API keeps the only copy of a user’s session in one instance’s memory. What complicates scale-out?

choices.text: Horizontal scaling always routes every user to one unchanged process.
A load balancer converts private sessions into database transactions.
Later requests may reach another instance without that state.
Adding instances automatically merges all private process memory.

questions.explanation: Private state can tie requests to an instance. Stateless design or an appropriate shared state strategy avoids that assumption.

sources.title: Autoscaling guidance
sources.claim: Stateless service design avoids instance affinity, and queue workers must not assume which instance handles a message.

questions.prompt: A dependency repeatedly times out and the circuit is open. What is the breaker’s primary action?

choices.text: Restart every unrelated service before allowing any local response.
Reject calls quickly rather than repeatedly invoking the failing dependency.
Retry every request indefinitely with no recovery limit.
Treat each timeout as success and clear the failure count.

questions.explanation: The open state avoids waste and repeated likely failures. A limited half-open probe can later test recovery; the breaker is distinct from unbounded retries.

sources.title: Circuit Breaker pattern
sources.claim: Closed allows calls, open rejects calls likely to fail, and half-open permits limited probes to decide whether recovery occurred.

questions.prompt: A collaborative editor must send frequent client edits and receive server updates over one connection. Which transport characteristic fits?

choices.text: A WebSocket supports both directions on the connection.
EventSource sends client edits through its receive stream.
SSE data fields automatically become client POST requests.
A one-way transport guarantees client edits reach the server.

questions.explanation: WebSocket supports sending and receiving. SSE requires a separate client-to-server mechanism and does not transform incoming fields into writes.

sources.title: WebSocket API
sources.claim: WebSocket supports bidirectional communication, while SSE is one-way server push.

sources.title: Using server-sent events
sources.claim: WebSocket supports bidirectional communication, while SSE is one-way server push.

questions.prompt: An SSE server sends retry: 3000. What does that field control?

choices.text: A three-second expiration of every user authentication token.
The maximum number of buffered events before the stream reconnects.
The required interval between every server-generated event.
A three-second delay before reconnection after loss.

questions.explanation: The retry field is an integer reconnection delay in milliseconds, so 3000 means three seconds. It is not token expiration, buffer capacity or the required interval between server events.

sources.title: Using server-sent events
sources.claim: The SSE retry field is an integer reconnection delay in milliseconds.

questions.prompt: Which transport distinctions hold? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Server-sent events carry server-to-client events over EventSource.
EventSource sends client-to-server events through the same event stream.
WebSocket is inherently receive-only like EventSource.
Every notification feature requires a bidirectional transport.
WebSocket can send data and receive server messages.

questions.explanation: A is correct: The event stream is one-way. B is incorrect: Client writes need a separate request mechanism. C is incorrect: It has a send operation. D is incorrect: One-way events can fit server-push notifications. E is correct: It supports two-way communication.

questions.prompt: Which SSE format and reconnection claims hold? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The retry field specifies integer milliseconds for reconnection.
A data field must contain a complete binary WebSocket frame.
An event field is always delivered to onmessage regardless of its name.
Serve the stream with the text/event-stream MIME type.
Separate complete event blocks with a blank line.

questions.explanation: A is correct: Non-integer values are ignored. B is incorrect: SSE uses text fields rather than WebSocket framing. C is incorrect: Named events use listeners for the specified event name. D is correct: It identifies an SSE response. E is correct: The delimiter finishes an event block.

sources.title: Using server-sent events
sources.claim: SSE uses text/event-stream with blank-line-separated events; retry specifies milliseconds and EventSource reconnects after disconnection.

questions.prompt: Which choices support scaling services across instances? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Treat private process memory as automatically shared after scale-out.
Require permanent instance affinity as the definition of statelessness.
Avoid assuming a user’s requests always reach the same instance.
Avoid assuming one fixed worker processes each queued message.
Store the only durable job progress in a terminating worker’s memory.

questions.explanation: A is incorrect: Instances do not merge their heaps. B is incorrect: Stateless design aims to avoid that routing dependency. C is correct: Scaling can change routing and instance availability. D is correct: A consumer pool can grow and shrink. E is incorrect: Scale-in can lose private state.

sources.title: Autoscaling guidance
sources.claim: Stateless service design avoids instance affinity, and queue workers must not assume which instance handles a message.

questions.prompt: Which breaker-state statements hold? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A breaker and a retry policy have identical purposes.
Closed normally permits calls while recording failures.
Open rejects calls while the dependency is considered unhealthy.
Half-open permits limited calls to test recovery.
Open requires every caller to retry continuously without delay.

questions.explanation: A is incorrect: Retry seeks eventual success; a breaker suppresses likely failures. B is correct: Failures can trigger transition to open. C is correct: It prevents repeated likely failures. D is correct: Probe results determine whether to close or reopen. E is incorrect: The breaker blocks attempts rather than causing an unlimited loop.

sources.title: Circuit Breaker pattern
sources.claim: Closed allows calls, open rejects calls likely to fail, and half-open permits limited probes to decide whether recovery occurred.
